name: Beau-Rivage Geneva
positioning: Lakefront hotel on Geneva's Quai du Mont-Blanc, open since 1865, owned by the Mayer family for 155 years and by the Casacuberta family since the end of 2020
best_for: Travelers who want a base on the Quai du Mont-Blanc facing Lake Geneva and the Jet d'Eau
History lovers drawn to the story of Empress Elisabeth of Austria
Guests who need a wheelchair-accessible hotel

facts.text: Beau-Rivage Geneva is at 13 quai du Mont-Blanc in Geneva.
The hotel faces Lake Geneva from the Quai du Mont-Blanc, looking across to the Jet d'Eau.
The Mayer family owned the hotel for 155 years.
At the end of 2020 the Mayers sold the hotel to another family, the Casacubertas.
Rooms mix Victorian, Edwardian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco design elements, and vary in mood from room to room.
Le Chat-Botte, the main fine-dining restaurant, opened in 1967.
Le Patara, downstairs, is a Thai restaurant.
The hotel uses GeniLac, a network that uses Lake Geneva water to cool and heat buildings.
The entire hotel is wheelchair-accessible, with special entrances off the Quai du Mont-Blanc to the lobby and key public areas.
Baby cots are free with prior reservation.
Pets are accepted with the hotel's prior approval, at an extra charge.

highlights.text: In 1898 Empress Elisabeth of Austria, a guest at the hotel, was stabbed outside it and died in her suite shortly after.
A cabinet holds a pair of Empress Elisabeth's gloves and a piece of bloodstained ribbon.
The outdoor restaurant La Terrasse becomes La Terrasse Alpine in winter, with heated vintage gondola cabins from Gstaad.
The hotel holds more than 150 angels in various forms, painted, sculpted and carved.
Albertine's, the little bar off the lobby, was formerly a reading room.

considerations.text: The spa is a single treatment room, the Bellefontaine Suite, where one therapist looks after one guest at a time.
Rooms are available from 3 p.m. on arrival day and must be vacated by noon on departure day.
The Geneva cantonal tourist tax is charged on top of the room rate.
